title: cost-opt: autotune batching/caching defaults + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds autotuning for batching and caching defaults, new quantization profiles for xformers and quant-llm, and a unit-economics diagnostics tool in the console. Expected median token cost reduction ~18% for common conversational workloads. No API surface changes.
description: Context: This PR implements the second phase of cost-optimization automation: (1) autotune conservative batching and KV-cache defaults per model/workload, (2) ship curated quantization profiles and heuristics for popular open models, and (3) add a unit-economics diagnostics tool that surfaces per-route token cost and recommended config changes. Motivation: customers running bursty conversational traffic have been overprovisioning batch sizes and leaving caching disabled; combined with stale quant defaults this increases unit cost. This work ties runtime heuristics to UEcon tooling to recommend and apply safe defaults. Changes summary: - runtime/autotune: add AutotuneCoordinator that samples latency/cost signals and computes recommended batch_size, max_latency_slo, and cache_enabled defaults per model tag; conservative rollback window and canary rollout support. - runtime/batching: add adaptive_batcher logic to honor per-route recommendations and enforce permitted ranges; include metrics hooks. - runtime/cache: KVCachePolicy improvements to allow hot-prefix detection and automatic small-cache enabling for short prompt reuse. - models/quant-profiles: add curated profiles for gpt2-xl-like, llama-2-13b, and open-llama variants; include tests and profile metadata. - console/uecon: new diagnostics panel showing per-route token cost, spend trend, and one-click apply suggestions (create a config change PR via platform). - e2e and unit tests: autotune unit tests, integration harness for batching under load, quant profile validation harness. Commits: 1) initial autotune coordinator and config schema 2) adaptive batcher integration and metrics 3) KV cache heuristics + tests 4) quant profile additions and profile validator 5) console UI + backend endpoints 6) e2e adjustments and flake fixes Files changed (high level): - runtime/autotune/*: new autotune coordinator, config proto, and tests - runtime/batching/*: adaptive_batcher.{rs,py} and tests - runtime/cache/*: kv_cache_policy.{rs,py} - models/quant-profiles/*.json: 6 profiles and validator - console/uecon/*: UI + api endpoints - docs: updated cost-optimization guide and rollout playbook Review conversation highlights: - Ravi: requested clearer invariants for safe rollback and a shorter canary window; author updated coordinator to add a 10-minute canary and explicit rollback reason codes. - Lina: asked for quant profile validation and a guard to prevent applying profiles that degrade perplexity beyond threshold; added profile-validator and a 2% eval quality guard. - Ethan: requested additional telemetry around trimmed tokens and cache hit ratio; added metrics and dashboard links. CI and testing: initial CI run reported two flaky e2e failures on the integration harness (race in test harness). Follow-ups fixed harness timing and retriggers passed all checks (unit, integration, lint, fmt). Performance results: internal canary on staging across three customers showed median per-token cost reduction of 12-25% depending on workload; latency P95 stayed within configured SLOs with the autotuned conservative defaults. Rollout plan and safety: - Canary rollout to 10% of routes for 48 hours with automated rollback on SLO violation (>5% increase in P95 latency) or quality regression (>2% perplexity). - Manual approval required before expanding to Dedicated environments. QA notes: ran smoke on Private installer and Verified no backward-incompatible config changes. Migration: existing routes keep current behavior until a tenant opts in or the Platform admin enables autotune globally. CLI/SDK: no API changes; console export creates a change PR that admins can review. Related: ENG-8123 (autotune design), ENG-8290 (quant profiles vetting). Known limitations: - Rare models with nonstandard KV behavior may need manual tuning; operator docs updated. - Quant profiles currently target 4/8-bit quant backends supported by our runtime; additional backends to follow. Merge outcome: squashed and merged after approvals from reviewers and CI passing. Author followups: will monitor telemetry and open follow-up PRs to add more model profiles and a visual diff of generation quality in the console. Checklist: [x] design doc linked (Linear ENG-8123) [x] unit tests added [x] integration tests for canary path [x] quant profile validator [x] console E2E smoke [x] docs updated
notes: Follow-up action: instrument an automated A/B evaluation for quality vs quant profile changes (ENG-8356). Monitor cost dashboard for 2 weeks post-rollout.
